title: Ill-conditioned Coulomb-metric Gram block was inverted silently; reject on min/max eigenvalue ratio < 1e-8
symptom: Remote RED test 3267914 showed the old code did not raise for the nearly singular Gram/Coulomb-metric block B = [[1, 1], [0, 1e-7]] (7 pass / 1 fail): a rank-deficient Gram matrix was inverted without any warning, so the resulting local RI fitting coefficients were garbage.
root_cause: The Coulomb-metric overlap (Gram) matrix used to obtain the local RI fitting coefficients becomes numerically singular for ill-conditioned auxiliary sets (heavy elements, high angular momentum, long atom-pair separations). A plain LU inverse guarded only by a relative pseudo-inverse threshold (exx_cs_inv_thr) hides the loss of accuracy instead of flagging it; the 1e-7 case passes the relative test but has an eigenvalue ratio far below anything invertible.
minimal_fix: Keep the original LU arithmetic, copy the Gram matrix and run the reused Hermitian eigensolver on the copy, then reject when min/max eigenvalue ratio < 1e-8; add the ratio as an optional output/status line. Use this together with exx_cs_inv_thr, not as a replacement for it.
validation: Re-run the RED case B = [[1, 1], [0, 1e-7]] and require a hard failure; add a well-conditioned control that must still pass; confirm the new status line reports the min/max ratio and that the archived v2 build turns the RED test green.
avoid: Do not rely on the relative pseudo-inverse threshold alone (it did not throw for the 1e-7 case) and do not silently regularize the Gram matrix in place.
